title: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham Promises 'More Breathing Room'
summary:
Andy Burnham is the new prime minister of the United Kingdom! He will give his first speech on Monday outside 10 Downing Street. In his speech, he promises to give people "more breathing room" — that means he wants to make life easier, especially with the cost of living.

Burnham was the mayor of Greater Manchester before becoming PM. He is the seventh prime minister in the last 10 years, so he wants to bring stability. He plans to scrap the idea of a government-issued digital ID for all adults. He also wants to take water and energy companies under public control, meaning the government would run them instead of private companies.

But some people are not happy. Environmental campaigners say he should stick to his promise not to issue new licenses for oil and gas drilling in the North Sea. They say drilling won't lower energy bills. Burnham has a lot of work to do, but he says he will be honest about the challenges.
why_it_matters: When a new leader takes charge, their decisions can change what your family pays for electricity and water, and even how much pocket money you might get, so it’s good to know what they promise.

background_read: The United Kingdom (UK) is made up of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. Its leader is called the prime minister, who lives at 10 Downing Street in London.
In recent years, the UK has had many prime ministers because of political changes, which has made people worried about the country's direction.
The 'cost of living crisis' means that prices for food, heating, and rent have gone up a lot, making it harder for families to afford everyday things.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andy Burnham, the new prime minister of the United Kingdom, formerly the mayor of Greater Manchester.
WHAT: He promised 'more breathing room' for people, meaning he wants to make life more affordable and stable, and plans to cancel digital ID and take control of water and energy companies.
WHERE: His first speech will be outside 10 Downing Street, London.
WHY: Because the UK has had many changes in leadership, and many people are struggling with high costs, so he aims to bring stability and relief.

perspectives.description: They think he will bring calm and fairness, lower energy bills, and stop unnecessary rules like digital IDs.
They are upset because they worry that new oil and gas drilling could harm the planet, and they don't believe it will actually make energy cheaper.
They are waiting to see if Burnham can really deliver what he promises, as many past leaders said similar things but didn't change much.
